summary: Surface stage complete. Mapped DVWA v1.10 *Development* at http://127.0.0.1:8080. Found 4 auth surfaces, 14 vulnerability module endpoints, 6 info-disclosure surfaces, 2 file-inclusion vectors, and static assets. Default credentials admin:password confirmed. Identified bookable candidates for SQL injection, command injection, CSRF, file upload, stored/reflected/DOM XSS, file inclusion, CSP bypass, JavaScript logic, weak session IDs, and brute force via source code disclosure.

candidates.title: SQL Injection (low) in /vulnerabilities/sqli/
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Source code confirms direct injection: $query = "SELECT * FROM `users` WHERE user = '$user' AND password = '$pass';"; $result = mysqli_query($GLOBALS["___mysqli_ston"], $query) or die('

');
candidates.poc_hint: Try id=1' OR '1'='1 or id=1 UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6

candidates.title: Command Injection (low) in /vulnerabilities/exec/
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST form with ip parameter for ping. Likely passes to shell_exec without sanitization. Form action='#' method='post', input name='ip' size='30'.

candidates.title: CSRF Password Change in /vulnerabilities/csrf/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Form uses GET method with password_new and password_conf fields, no CSRF token visible in the form. <form action="#" method="GET"> <input type="password" name="password_new"> <input type="password" name="password_conf"> <input type="submit" value="Change" name="Change">
candidates.poc_hint: Submit GET request with password_new=attacker123&password_conf=attacker123&Change=Change as victim

candidates.title: File Upload (low) in /vulnerabilities/upload/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Upload form with enctype='multipart/form-data', hidden MAX_FILE_SIZE=100000, file input name='uploaded'. Upload directory confirmed writable: /var/www/html/hackable/uploads/ [User: www-data] Writable folder Yes.
candidates.poc_hint: Upload a PHP file (e.g., shell.php) and access at /hackable/uploads/shell.php

candidates.title: Reflected XSS (low) in /vulnerabilities/xss_r/
candidates.proof_excerpt: X-XSS-Protection header set to 0, name parameter reflected in page. <form name="XSS" action="#" method="GET"> <input type="text" name="name"> <input type="submit" value="Submit">
candidates.poc_hint: Try ?name=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>

candidates.title: Stored XSS (low) in /vulnerabilities/xss_s/
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Guestbook form with txtName and mtxMessage parameters. Existing comment shows:
Name: test
Message: This is a test comment.
candidates.poc_hint: POST txtName=<script>alert(1)</script>&mtxMessage=<script>alert(2)</script>&btnSign=Sign+Guestbook

candidates.title: DOM XSS (low) in /vulnerabilities/xss_d/
candidates.proof_excerpt: JavaScript reads from URL: if (document.location.href.indexOf("default=") >= 0) { var lang = document.location.href.substring(document.location.href.indexOf("default=")+8); document.write("<option value='" + lang + "'>" + decodeURI(lang) + "</option>"); }
candidates.poc_hint: Use URL fragment: #default=<script>alert(1)</script>

candidates.title: Local File Inclusion in /vulnerabilities/fi/
candidates.proof_excerpt: File inclusion module with page parameter. Links: file1.php, file2.php, file3.php. Warning: allow_url_include disabled. [file1.php] - [file2.php] - [file3.php]
candidates.poc_hint: Try ?page=../../../../etc/passwd or ?page=../../../../proc/self/environ

candidates.title: File Inclusion in /instructions.php via doc parameter
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Instructions submenu with doc parameter:
Read MePDF GuideChange LogCopyingPHPIDS License
candidates.poc_hint: Try ?doc=../../../../etc/passwd (LFI via include)

candidates.title: Insecure CAPTCHA / Logic Bypass in /vulnerabilities/captcha/
candidates.proof_excerpt: reCAPTCHA API key missing from config. Hidden step parameter. <form action="#" method="POST" style="display:none;"> <input type="hidden" name="step" value="1" /> New password: <input type="password" name="password_new"> Confirm: <input type="password" name="password_conf">
candidates.poc_hint: Try submitting step=2 (bypass captcha check) with password_new=test&password_conf=test

candidates.title: Weak Session IDs in /vulnerabilities/weak_id/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Generates dvwaSession cookie on POST. Predictable session ID generation. <form method="post"> <input type="submit" value="Generate" /> </form>
candidates.poc_hint: Generate multiple sessions and analyze dvwaSession cookie pattern

candidates.title: CSP Bypass in /vulnerabilities/csp/
candidates.proof_excerpt: CSP header: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com . Form accepts include parameter for external JS URL. <form name="csp" method="POST"> <input size="50" type="text" name="include" value=""> <input type="submit" value="Include" /> </form>
candidates.poc_hint: Use allowed CDN (code.jquery.com) or pastebin to host malicious JS

candidates.title: JavaScript Logic Bypass in /vulnerabilities/javascript/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Client-side validation: token = md5(rot13(phrase)). Phrase must equal 'success' but token is computed client-side via JS. <form name="low_js" method="post"> <input type="hidden" name="token" value="" id="token" /> <input type="text" name="phrase" value="ChangeMe" id="phrase" /> <input type="submit" id="send" name="send" value="Submit" /> </form>
candidates.poc_hint: Compute md5(rot13('success')) and submit directly, or bypass client-side check

candidates.title: Brute Force (low) in /vulnerabilities/brute/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Source code shows direct SQL injection in query: $query = "SELECT * FROM `users` WHERE user = '$user' AND password = '$pass';"; md5(password) used. No CSRF token. No rate limiting.
candidates.poc_hint: SQL injection via username or password field, or brute force with dictionary

raw.summary: Surface stage complete. Mapped DVWA v1.10 *Development* at http://127.0.0.1:8080. Found 4 auth surfaces, 14 vulnerability module endpoints, 6 info-disclosure surfaces, 2 file-inclusion vectors, and static assets. Default credentials admin:password confirmed. Identified bookable candidates for SQL injection, command injection, CSRF, file upload, stored/reflected/DOM XSS, file inclusion, CSP bypass, JavaScript logic, weak session IDs, and brute force via source code disclosure.

surfaces.note: Main login form with CSRF token protection. Default creds admin:password work. Sets PHPSESSID and security cookies.
Logout, redirects to login.php
Database setup/reset. Reveals MySQL creds, writable paths, PHP settings. CSRF token present.
Security level settings (low/medium/high/impossible). PHPIDS toggle. IDS log viewer link.
Full PHP configuration disclosure: PHP 7.0.30, Apache 2.4.25 (Debian), Linux x86_64
PHPIDS log viewer. Log file at /var/www/html/external/phpids/0.6/lib/IDS/tmp/phpids_log.txt
Instructions page with file inclusion via ?doc= parameter (readme, PDF, changelog, copying, PHPIDS-license)
File Inclusion module. allow_url_include disabled (LFI only). Pages: include.php, file1.php, file2.php, file3.php
Brute Force login - direct SQL query with md5(password). Source shows no CSRF protection.
Command Injection via ping. Takes IP address and likely passes to shell_exec/passthru.
CSRF password change. GET request with password_new/password_conf - no CSRF token.
File upload with multipart form. Uploads to /var/www/html/hackable/uploads/
Insecure CAPTCHA password change. reCAPTCHA key missing. Step parameter controls logic flow.
SQL Injection - GET parameter ID passed directly into SQL query (source code confirmed).
SQL Injection Blind - GET parameter ID, same pattern as sqli.
Weak Session IDs - generates dvwaSession cookie on POST.
DOM XSS - default parameter read from URL via document.location.href and written directly to DOM.
Reflected XSS - name parameter reflected in page. X-XSS-Protection header set to 0.
Stored XSS - guestbook with name/message stored and displayed. Maxlength 10/50 chars.
CSP Bypass - accepts external script URL. CSP: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com
JavaScript Attacks - phrase field validated via MD5(rot13(phrase)) token to submit 'success'.
Source code disclosure for specific module and security level.
Source code comparison across all security levels.
Help page for each vulnerability module.
Writable upload directory confirmed via setup.php. Used by file upload module.
Writable PHPIDS log file confirmed via setup.php.
Writable config directory confirmed via setup.php. Contains config.inc.php with DB credentials.
Disallow: /
